jobs.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: transparent natural-history game sprite animation atlas, replacing crude pixel art in a painterly lake game. Match finely illustrated realistic watercolor/gouache wildlife with delicate feather detail and softly painted edges, the same polished hand-painted style as realistic butterfly specimen sprites. This is NOT pixel art, NOT a flat vector icon, NOT a cartoon. Produce ONE exact 4-column by 3-row regular atlas with TWELVE equal rectangular cells on genuinely transparent RGBA background. Each cell contains the SAME individual bird, same body proportions, same center of chest at the cell center, fixed camera, constant apparent size. Every pose fully contained, wings and tail never clipped, with at least 10% clear margin and transparent gutters. No grid lines, text, labels, contact shadows, scenery, perch, water, glow or checkerboard. Native image detail sufficient for clean 192-pixel animation frames. Read left to right, top to bottom. Cells 1-8: one fluid flying wingbeat cycle, wings high raised, partially raised, level spread, partly down, fully down, partly down, level, partly raised. Bird stays in place; animate wings with anatomically plausible feather fans, do not resize the body. Cell 9: steady level-wing glide with relaxed feet tucked. Cells 10-12: progressive slowing/landing in flight, body pitches slightly upright, wings sweep up and forward, tail fans, feet extend then reach downward to settle. These three are distinct successive braking poses. Keep all twelve cells aligned and consistent. Subject: a male Northern cardinal, richly but naturally painted muted scarlet-red plumage, small pointed crest, black facial mask, warm orange conical beak, darker red flight feathers and long red tail. EXACT CAMERA: FRONT, head-on, bird flying TOWARD the viewer, face and both eyes visible symmetrically, red chest visible, wings extend left and right, tail recedes behind. Do not draw a side view. Soft neutral daylight, no hard outlines, natural lake-game colors.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target: the generated cardinal twelve-pose animation atlas. Keep this same bird's identity, species markings, realistic hand-painted feather style, color palette and twelve-pose sequence. Image 2 is a style reference only: the existing butterfly art. Change ONLY the bird's CAMERA DIRECTION in every pose to: FRONT LEFT, three-quarter front view: the bird flies toward the viewer and toward the LEFT side of the image. This is a three-dimensional oblique camera view, not a flat rotation of the original. Preserve the EXACT 4 columns x 3 rows layout and same constant scale and chest-centered placement. Render high-quality natural-history watercolor/gouache feather detail with smooth painted edges, matching the butterfly specimen artwork. No pixel-art blocks, no vector look, no caricature. True transparent background; no scenery, perches, shadow, labels, text, borders, grid or checkerboard. Maintain a steady body between wing poses; only wings articulate except the requested progressive landing posture.
